resources.string: How the erector spinae extends and supports the spine
Spinal extension and support

A simplified view from behind and from the side, with the front of the body to the right in side views. The scenes show normal anatomy; color changes illustrate relative demand, not measured muscle activity or force.
Paired columns beside the spine
Deep to the more superficial back muscles, the erector spinae runs along both sides of the vertebral column. From the midline outward, its columns are spinalis, longissimus and iliocostalis.
Both sides help extend the spine

As the trunk moves from slight spinal flexion toward neutral, the two sides of the erector spinae contribute together. The pelvis stays still in this view so the change in spinal curvature is visible.
Neutral with external support
The backrest takes some of the demand for holding the trunk in place. The spine keeps its natural curves, and the back muscles can still be active.
Neutral under an external load
Here a load in front of the trunk tends to bend the spine forward. The spinal extensors can contribute more to resisting that tendency without creating a larger arch or visible spinal extension.
